question: Do two full verify.ps1 runs, launched at the same time from two different worktrees with no -TemporaryRoot, both go green?
method: Checked out the committed fix (61b7e00) in both C:/gamedev/_wt-302 (the claimed worktree) and C:/gamedev/_wt-302-repro-b (a throwaway worktree created for this reproduction, sibling to the claimed one, removed after use).

Launched both full runs in the same message so they start together: 'powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1 -GodotPath C:/gamedev/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64_console.exe' with no -TemporaryRoot, from each worktree.

Confirmed both processes were live and progressing through stages concurrently by polling each run's own stdout log before either finished (both showed distinct verification_temporary_root events - df-verify-4326b631 and df-verify-c0562c45 - before either reached its verification_result).
temporaryRootsDidNotCollide: df-verify-4326b631 (A) vs df-verify-c0562c45 (B) - distinct paths, same sibling-of-repository-root shape, no coordination needed between the two runs.

cleanupResult.B: C:\gamedev\df-verify-c0562c45 confirmed absent immediately after the run finished (Test-Path -> False).
cleanupResult.A: C:\gamedev\df-verify-4326b631 was NOT fully removed. verify.ps1 reported it as a warning, not a failure, and still returned status ok: {"event":"temporary_cleanup","status":"warning","description":"own temporary root directory","path":"C:\\gamedev\\df-verify-4326b631","reason":"\u041e\u0442\u043a\u0430\u0437\u0430\u043d\u043e \u0432 \u0434\u043e\u0441\u0442\u0443\u043f\u0435 \u043f\u043e \u043f\u0443\u0442\u0438 \"System.Text.Json.SourceGeneration.dll\"."}. Cause: several long-lived 'dotnet.exe' MSBuild/Roslyn node-reuse worker processes were still running on the shared machine afterward and holding a handle open inside that run's isolated DOTNET_CLI_HOME, which lives under the temporary root. This is the exact scenario Issue #89's best-effort cleanup design exists for - a directory that stops being deletable for a reason outside the run's control after the preflight already proved it usable - and it behaved as designed: warning in the structured output, run still status ok. Not fixed here (out of scope: this is dotnet's own node-reuse holding a lock, not something this Issue's default-directory change introduced or could prevent without disabling node reuse, a broader and unmeasured behaviour change). The leftover directory was left in place rather than force-killing the shared machine's dotnet processes, since two other tasks (#301, #303) were running on the same machine at the time and those processes could not be attributed to this session alone.
